title: Chain Traversal

story.briefing: Below the network the relays are chained, each holding only the address of the next. There is no index — the only way through is to follow the links.
story.success: Chain walked end to end. Every relay reports in.

description: A chain is given as an array of nodes and a starting index. Each node is a two-element array [value, next], where next is the index of the following node, or -1 at the end of the chain. The head may be -1, meaning the chain is empty. Return the sum of all values along the chain. An empty chain sums to 0.
constraints: 0 <= nodes.length <= 300000, -1000 <= value <= 1000, the chain never revisits a node

examples.explanation: Node 0 holds 5 and points to node 2, which holds 4 and points to node 1, which holds 9.

hints: The order of the nodes in the array tells you nothing. Only the next field decides where you go, and the chain usually does not run left to right.
You need a variable holding your current position, not a loop counter over the array. The loop ends when that position becomes -1, not when it reaches the array length.
Set a position to head and a total to 0. While the position is not -1, add that node value to the total and set the position to the node next field. Return the total.
